patients.summary: IT specialist who joined in 2021 healthy apart from a mild chronic anemia. Develops sarcoidosis with erythema nodosum (2023), primary adrenal insufficiency on replacement (2024), and in 2025 necrolytic migratory erythema that leads to a glucagonoma of the pancreatic tail, resected with splenectomy in December 2025.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
43M here to establish. Transferring from another primary care office; records requested. Works in IT, mostly desk work. Feels well. No meds, no supplements. NKDA.

PMH: nothing chronic that he knows of.
PSH: appendectomy at 16, no complications.
FH: father with type 2 diabetes. Mother with autoimmune thyroiditis. One sister with pulmonary sarcoidosis, doing OK.
SH: married, lives in Easthampton. Never smoked. Drinks socially, a beer or two a week. No formal exercise.

ROS negative across the board: no chest pain, SOB, cough, GI or GU complaints, no weight change, sleeping fine.

Exam: well appearing. BP and HR as recorded. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement or nodules. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed RLQ scar. Skin without rash. Ext no edema. Mood and affect normal.

COVID: two Pfizer doses this spring at a pharmacy (card seen). Last tetanus he can't recall -> Tdap today.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c (father with DM), TSH (mother's thyroid), one-time HIV and hep C screens. Colon screening discussed, he'll be due at 45. Flu shot in the fall.
2. Diet/activity: brief counseling, aim for 150 min/wk.

RTC 1 yr for physical, sooner prn.

documents.title: MA Intake
documents.author: MA
documents.body: New pt intake. Vitals obtained. Med list reviewed: none. Allergies: NKDA, confirmed. PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2. Pt brought COVID card, 2 doses entered as historical. Release of information signed for prior PCP office.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jamal, your labs look good overall: kidney and liver tests, sugar (A1c), cholesterol and thyroid are all normal, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Your hemoglobin is a touch low at 12.4, with normal-sized red cells. That isn't anything to act on right now, but I'd like to recheck it at your physical next year. Let me know if you ever notice unusual tiredness, shortness of breath, or dark stools before then.

documents.title: RE: Your recent labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks doc. Sounds good, I'll get the physical on the calendar.

documents.author: front desk

Received 14 pages by fax from patient's former primary care office (records dated 2012 through 2020). Scanned to chart.

Summary for provider: yearly physicals, last 2020-02. Problem list blank. Surgical hx appendectomy as a teenager. No medications. Allergies none recorded. Lipids and glucose normal on file. Flu shots most years. No specialist referrals.

Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Outside Records Review

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Doing well. Busy year at work. Sleeping 7 h. No fatigue he'd call out of the ordinary. No bleeding, no dark or bloody stools, eats meat a few times a week. No NSAID use.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Exam: NAD. Vitals reviewed. Conjunctivae pink. Neck no LAD, thyroid normal. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abd soft, NT, no HSM. Skin clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Hgb 12.4 last year, normocytic. Repeat CBC w/ diff today plus iron studies, B12, folate.
2. Preventive: CMP, lipids, A1c. Flu shot this fall + updated COVID booster when available. Colonoscopy next year at 45.

RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 11.9, MCV 83, rest of the CBC unremarkable. Iron, ferritin, B12 and folate all normal. Second mildly low value a year apart with nothing to chase on iron or vitamins. Will carry as chronic mild normocytic anemia and trend yearly. CMP, lipids, A1c normal. Messaged pt.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count is still mildly low (hemoglobin 11.9) but your iron, B12 and folate levels are all normal, so there's no deficiency to treat. I've added it to your problem list as a mild long-standing anemia, and we'll keep an eye on it every year. Everything else, including cholesterol and sugar, is normal.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 45 yo M.

Interval: dry cough on and off since around April. No fever, no sputum, no blood, no wheeze or chest tightness. Had a cold going around the house in the spring and thinks it started then. Some throat clearing in the mornings. Never smoker, no vaping. No heartburn. No new meds (none at all). Energy fine.

Exam: well, not coughing during the visit. Oropharynx clear. Lungs clear throughout, no crackles or wheeze. Heart RRR. Abd benign. Skin clear. No LAD.

A/P
1. Cough ~2 mo, nonsmoker, normal exam: most likely post-viral or postnasal drip. Watchful waiting; saline rinses. If still going past the 8-week mark or any fever/SOB/weight loss, let me know and we'll go further.
2. Chronic mild anemia: recheck CBC.
3. Prostate screening: discussed starting at 45 given higher risk in Black men; he wants a PSA. Ordered.
4. Colon cancer screening due now: GI referral for colonoscopy.
5. CMP, lipids, A1c.

RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 11.4, normocytic, a little lower than last year, still mild. PSA 0.8. A1c, lipids, CMP normal. Will keep trending. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside endoscopy center. Procedure date 2023-08-08.
Indication: average-risk colorectal cancer screening, age 45.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep: Boston Bowel Prep Scale 8 (3/3/2).
Findings: cecum reached and confirmed by appendiceal orifice area and ileocecal valve; post-appendectomy appearance. Normal mucosa throughout the colon on withdrawal. No polyps.
Impression: normal screening colonoscopy.
Recommendation: repeat in 10 years.

orders.reason: Chronic dry cough, sister with pulmonary sarcoidosis

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from his home office.

Cough still there, ~4 months now. Dry, worse talking for long stretches on calls. Saline rinses didn't change it. More tired than usual the last few weeks, he figured from the cough and work. No fever, sweats, hemoptysis, chest pain, SOB on stairs. No new pets or hobbies, no travel.

He brought up his sister, who has pulmonary sarcoidosis, and asked whether this could be the same.

Obs on video: speaking full sentences, occasional dry cough, no distress.

A/P: Chronic dry cough in a nonsmoker, now well past the post-viral window, with a sister who has sarcoid. Referring straight to pulmonology for evaluation and imaging rather than piecemeal here. He's fine with that. Call sooner for fever, blood, or breathing trouble.

reports.text: PA and lateral views of the chest. Comparison: none. The hila are bilaterally full, compatible with hilar lymph node enlargement. Lungs are clear without focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contour otherwise normal. Osseous structures intact.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary clinic. Seen 2023-10-05.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for referring Mr. Robinson, 45, for chronic cough.

He describes about six months of nonproductive cough with generalized fatigue. Over the last two weeks painful red bumps have come up on both shins. No fever, hemoptysis, chest pain or recent infection. He has never been told he had tuberculosis, recalls no fungal exposures (no caving, construction dust, birds) and has not traveled recently. Never smoker; social alcohol; works in IT. No medications. NKDA. Appendectomy as a teen. Family: his sister has pulmonary sarcoidosis; father with type 2 diabetes; mother with autoimmune thyroiditis.

Exam: vital signs normal. Several tender erythematous nodules over both anterior tibial surfaces. Faint crackles at both bases, no wheeze. No clubbing. No palpable peripheral adenopathy. Heart regular. No hepatosplenomegaly.

Data: hemoglobin 10.5, MCV 82. Chest radiograph today shows bilateral hilar fullness.

Impression: subacute cough with bilateral hilar adenopathy and lesions typical of erythema nodosum. Sarcoidosis is the leading consideration, particularly with his family history; lymphoma and granulomatous infection need to be excluded.

Plan: bronchoscopy with sampling of the hilar nodes, scheduled for 10/19. I'll write again once pathology is back.

With thanks,
Pulmonology

reports.text:
Specimen: bilateral hilar lymph nodes, transbronchial sampling.
Gross: multiple tan tissue fragments and core material, submitted entirely.
Microscopic: lymph node tissue containing multiple well-formed non-caseating epithelioid granulomas with scattered multinucleated giant cells. No necrosis. AFB and GMS stains negative for organisms. No malignant cells.
reports.conclusion: Hilar lymph nodes: non-caseating granulomatous inflammation; special stains negative for acid-fast bacilli and fungi. No malignancy.

documents.title: Bronchoscopy Procedure Note
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside hospital bronchoscopy suite, 2023-10-19.
Indication: bilateral hilar adenopathy.
Anesthesia: moderate sedation with topical lidocaine.
Airway inspection: normal to the subsegmental level bilaterally, no endobronchial lesions.
Sampling: transbronchial needle passes from right and left hilar nodes; rapid on-site evaluation showed lymphocytes and granulomas.
Complications: none. Discharged home same day.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary clinic.

Dear Doctor,

The hilar node samples from Mr. Robinson's bronchoscopy on 10/19 show non-caseating granulomas, with stains negative for mycobacteria and fungi and no malignant cells. Together with the bilateral hilar adenopathy and erythema nodosum, this fits sarcoidosis.

I spoke with him by phone today. This presentation tends to settle on its own, so I am not starting treatment. We will watch the cough and skin and see him back in the spring, sooner if he worsens. He knows to call with breathing trouble.

With thanks,
Pulmonology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after pulm workup. Bronch 10/19, nodes with non-caseating granulomas, stains neg -> sarcoidosis per pulm, observation only. He's relieved it isn't cancer.

Cough the same, maybe slightly less. Shin bumps fading, less tender. Tired. No fevers. Eyes fine, no redness or blurring.

Exam: shins with a few faint violaceous macules, no active tender nodules. Lungs: no crackles appreciated today. Heart RRR.

Hgb 10.5 on pulm's CBC, MCV 82, down from 11.4 in June. Known chronic mild normocytic anemia, iron and vitamins were normal last year.

A/P
1. Sarcoidosis, pulm following, no treatment. Pulm f/u in spring.
2. Chronic anemia, a bit lower. Recheck with physical; low threshold for repeat iron studies.
3. Flu + updated COVID today.

documents.title: Cough update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just a quick update for my file. The bumps on my legs are totally gone and the cough has calmed way down, maybe once or twice a day now. Still more tired than I'd like but I'll take it. Pulm appointment is next month.

documents.title: RE: Cough update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great to hear, thanks for letting me know. Keep the pulmonology visit. If the tiredness doesn't keep improving, bring it up at your physical and we'll take a look.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary clinic. Seen 2024-03-21.

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Robinson returns for sarcoidosis. His cough is much less frequent and the erythema nodosum has cleared. Some ongoing tiredness. No dyspnea, chest pain or eye symptoms.

Exam: vitals normal, oxygen saturation normal on room air. Lungs clear today. Shins clear.

Assessment: sarcoidosis, improving on observation alone. No indication for therapy.

Plan: continue observation; he will contact us if the cough returns or breathing changes.

With thanks,
Pulmonology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46M annual.

Sarcoid: cough basically gone, pulm in March said improving, observation. Shins clear.

Main complaint is fatigue, going on since last fall. Gets through the workday but wiped by evening, naps on weekends which isn't like him. Sleep 7 h, no snoring per wife. Mood OK, PHQ-9 3. Weight down ~2 kg since last year, not trying. Appetite "fine, maybe a little less."

Meds none. NKDA.

Exam: NAD. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abd soft. Skin: no rash, shins clear. Thyroid normal size. No LAD.

A/P
1. Fatigue: CBC, CMP, TSH (mother with thyroiditis), A1c. Could be anemia, could be lingering sarcoid. Recheck after labs.
2. Chronic mild anemia: trending.
3. Sarcoidosis: per pulm.
4. Prevention: colonoscopy 2023 normal, PSA 2023 normal, flu/COVID in fall.

RTC 1 yr, sooner if fatigue worsens.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jamal, thyroid, kidney, liver, electrolytes and sugar are all normal. Your hemoglobin is 11.0, similar to the past couple of years, so it doesn't fully explain how tired you've been. Some of this may be your body still settling after the sarcoidosis. Let's see how the summer goes; if you're not feeling better, or if the weight keeps coming off, book a visit and we'll dig further.

orders.reason: Fatigue, weakness, weight loss, hyperpigmentation; evaluate for adrenal insufficiency

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired and weak.

Fatigue now about a year and getting worse, not better as hoped. New over the summer: legs and arms feel weak, harder carrying groceries up the stairs. Weight down again without trying. Wife noticed his forearms and elbows have gotten darker over the past few months; he hadn't paid it attention. No fever, no cough to speak of, no abdominal pain, no vomiting.

Exam: tired-appearing. BP lower than his usual. Weight 78.5 (83 at baseline). Skin: darker pigmentation over forearms and elbows, more than sun-exposed elsewhere. No focal weakness on exam. Lungs clear. Heart RRR.

A/P: Progressive fatigue, weakness, weight loss, low-normal BP and new hyperpigmentation. Primary adrenal insufficiency has to be ruled out first. Urgent endocrinology referral, front desk to call for the soonest slot. CMP today.

Go to the ED for vomiting, fainting, confusion or severe abdominal pain. Discussed why.

documents.title: Referral Coordination
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Urgent endocrinology referral faxed with today's note. Endo office offered 9/30 at 9:15, earliest available; asked to be placed on cancellation list. Pt informed by phone and agreed.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CMP normal, sodium and potassium in range. Normal lytes don't exclude adrenal insufficiency. Keep the endo appt. Pt informed.

medications.sig: Take 1 and 1/2 tablets (15 mg) by mouth on waking
Take 1 tablet (5 mg) by mouth in the early afternoon
Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning
Inject 100 mg intramuscularly once for adrenal crisis or inability to keep oral steroids down, then call 911

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology practice. Seen 2024-09-30.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for the urgent referral of Mr. Robinson, 46, with sarcoidosis followed by pulmonology and no prior steroid exposure.

History: roughly a year of steadily worsening fatigue and generalized muscle weakness, unplanned weight loss, and several months of darkening over the forearms and elbows. No medications. NKDA.

Exam: BP 100/60, HR 82. Weight 78 kg. Increased pigmentation in the palmar creases and on the buccal mucosa. No goiter.

Labs: CBC with a mild normocytic anemia and eosinophils of 14%. A cosyntropin stimulation test done in our office showed only a very small rise in serum cortisol.

Impression: primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease).

Plan:
- Hydrocortisone 15 mg on waking and 5 mg in the early afternoon.
- Fludrocortisone 0.1 mg each morning.
- Hydrocortisone 100 mg IM emergency kit prescribed; injection technique taught.
- Sick-day rules: double oral doses for fever or significant illness, triple for high fever; injection and ED for vomiting.
- Medical alert ID recommended.
- Follow-up here in about 3 months.

With thanks,
Endocrinology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u new dx primary adrenal insufficiency (endo 9/30). On hydrocortisone 15 mg AM / 5 mg early afternoon, fludrocortisone 0.1 mg. Has the IM hydrocortisone kit at home, wife shown how to use it too.

One week in: "like someone turned the lights back on." Appetite better.

Exam: BP improved. Hyperpigmentation unchanged (expected to fade slowly).

A/P
1. Primary adrenal insufficiency: reviewed sick-day rules again, he can recite them. Med alert bracelet ordered online. Flagged in chart: stress-dose steroids for procedures/surgery. Endo f/u January.
2. Sarcoidosis: quiet.
3. Chronic anemia: recheck at physical.
4. Flu + COVID today.

documents.title: Pharmacy Refill Request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: refill request hydrocortisone 10 mg and 5 mg tabs, 90-day supply requested for mail order. Original Rx from endocrinology. Called endo office, they prefer to keep prescribing; they sent 90-day Rxs today. Pharmacy and pt notified.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology practice. Seen 2025-01-16.

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Robinson is doing well on replacement for primary adrenal insufficiency. Energy and strength are much improved and he has regained weight, now 80 kg. No illnesses requiring stress dosing so far. Pigmentation is lighter.

BP 116/72. Sodium and potassium normal on today's BMP.

Plan: continue hydrocortisone 15 mg on waking and 5 mg early afternoon, and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily. Emergency kit in date. Review sick-day rules annually. See us in about a year, sooner as needed.

With thanks,
Endocrinology

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
47M, annual.

Feels the best he has in a couple of years. Back to normal workdays, walking at lunch again.

Adrenal insufficiency: hydrocortisone 15/5, fludrocortisone 0.1. Endo Jan, no changes, next visit in a year. No stress doses needed. Wears his med alert bracelet.

Chronic anemia: no symptoms.

Exam: BP and weight reviewed, weight back up to 81. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abd soft, NT. Skin: residual faint darkening of palmar creases. Shins clear. No edema.

1. Preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c. Repeat PSA (shared decision, he prefers to keep checking).
2. Adrenal insufficiency: stable on replacement.
3. Sarcoidosis: quiescent.
4. Anemia: trend.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit. Rash on lower abdomen for about 3 weeks. Itchy and sore, worse with sweat and the waistband. Tried an OTC clotrimazole cream and then OTC hydrocortisone cream for about a week each, neither helped much. No fever.

On video and uploaded photo: red, scaly patch across the lower abdomen below the umbilicus, edges somewhat sharper than the center.

A/P: Likely intertrigo/fungal given location, summer, sweat. Rx ketoconazole 2% cream BID, keep area dry, loose waistband. If not clearly better in 3-4 weeks, come in so I can look in person.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rash f/u. Five weeks of ketoconazole, no real change, now spreading down into the groin. Painful more than itchy. Weight 78.5, down from 81 in May; he says he's been skipping lunch with a big project and not very hungry.

Exam: afebrile. Erythematous scaly patches lower abdomen extending to inguinal folds bilaterally, some crusting at edges. No vesicles. No satellite pustules.

A/P: Not behaving like tinea. Stop ketoconazole. Trial of triamcinolone 0.1% cream BID x 2 wk in case this is an eczematous/irritant process. If no better, dermatology. Recheck weight next visit.

orders.reason: Painful rash of lower abdomen, groin and perineum not responding to topical antifungal and steroid

documents.title: Rash still bad
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The steroid cream calmed it for a few days but it came right back and now it's spread back toward my bottom. It burns. Can I see a dermatologist? I've attached two pictures.

documents.title: RE: Rash still bad
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the photos, Jamal. Yes, this needs a dermatologist, and I've put the referral in today. Stop the triamcinolone in the meantime. Our front desk will call you with the appointment. If you get a fever or the skin opens up and drains, let me know right away.

documents.title: Referral Coordination
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Dermatology referral sent with notes and photos. First new-patient opening 10/14. Pt accepted, waitlisted for sooner.

reports.text:
Specimen: skin, left medial thigh at edge of plaque, 4 mm punch.
Microscopic: epidermis with confluent parakeratosis and pallor of the upper spinous layer with scattered necrotic keratinocytes. Superficial perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis. PAS stain negative for fungal elements.
reports.conclusion: Necrotic keratinocytes in the upper epidermis with perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate; no fungal organisms. See comment: in the right clinical setting the pattern is compatible with necrolytic migratory erythema.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology practice. Seen 2025-10-14.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for sending Mr. Robinson, 47, who carries diagnoses of sarcoidosis and primary adrenal insufficiency on hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. NKDA.

He has had a painful rash for four months that began on the lower abdomen and has moved into the groin and perineum despite several antifungal and steroid creams, none of which helped for long. He has lost about 8 kg over the past three months without trying, feels more tired, and has some mild abdominal discomfort. He has also had a dry mouth and been more thirsty lately, which he puts down to stress.

Exam: weight 73 kg. A large red, scaly plaque with crusted areas and central clearing across the lower abdomen and onto both medial thighs. Mild pallor of the conjunctivae.

Labs today: hemoglobin 10.2 with normocytic indices, glucose 212, ALT 64 and AST 52. HIV screen negative.

A punch biopsy was taken from the edge of the thigh plaque.

Impression: chronic, treatment-resistant eruption of the lower abdomen, groin and perineum with weight loss, anemia and hyperglycemia. I am concerned about necrolytic migratory erythema and will write again with the pathology.

With thanks,
Dermatology

documents.title: Dermatology Addendum
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology practice.

Dear Doctor,

The biopsy shows necrotic keratinocytes high in the epidermis with a perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate and no fungus. With the clinical picture of a migrating flexural rash, weight loss, anemia and a glucose of 212, this is most consistent with necrolytic migratory erythema.

Necrolytic migratory erythema is classically a sign of a glucagon-secreting pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. I would recommend a serum glucagon level and dedicated pancreatic imaging. I called Mr. Robinson today to explain and told him your office would be in touch.

With thanks,
Dermatology

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derm letters reviewed. Called pt, booked 10/20 AM, fasting. Will order glucagon and pancreas-protocol CT at that visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

orders.order: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast, pancreas protocol
orders.reason: Necrolytic migratory erythema, evaluate for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u derm. Biopsy + clinical picture read as necrolytic migratory erythema; derm recommends glucagon and pancreatic imaging to look for a glucagonoma.

Rash about 4 months: lower abdomen -> groin -> perineum. Painful. Weight 81 in May, 78.5 Aug, 73 at derm, 72.8 today. Tired, mild vague abdominal discomfort. Dry mouth and thirsty for a few weeks. Glucose 212 at derm. ALT 64 / AST 52, Hgb 10.2. Taking hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone as prescribed, no extra doses.

Exam: thin compared with spring. Mild conjunctival pallor. Abdomen soft, nontender, no mass or organomegaly. Skin: large scaly erythematous plaque lower abdomen into the inguinal folds and medial thighs with crusted edges.

A/P
1. Necrolytic migratory erythema with weight loss, hyperglycemia and anemia: glucagon level today, CT abd/pelvis pancreas protocol ASAP. Discussed with him plainly that this pattern can come from a hormone-producing pancreatic tumor; he asked good questions, wife on speaker.
2. Hyperglycemia: very likely part of the same process, on top of daily hydrocortisone. Not labeling diabetes yet, holding off on meds pending workup. Repeat CMP today. He'll call for polyuria worsening, vomiting or confusion.
3. Adrenal insufficiency: same doses. Emailed endo with derm findings so they're in the loop before any procedure.
4. Mildly elevated LFTs: recheck today, CT will look at liver.
5. Flu + COVID today.

Call with any questions.

documents.title: Result Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with glucagon 1,180 pg/mL (ref 50-150), markedly elevated. Fits the derm concern. CMP from 10/20: glucose still high, LFTs similar. CT booked 10/28. He understands the next step is finding where the tumor is. Spent 15 min.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Technique: multiphase CT of the abdomen with pancreatic protocol (late arterial and portal venous phases) and portal venous imaging of the pelvis after IV contrast. Indication: elevated glucagon, necrolytic migratory erythema.
Findings: There is a 3.4 x 2.9 cm solid mass in the pancreatic tail that enhances avidly in the arterial phase. The pancreatic duct is not dilated. The remainder of the pancreas is normal. Liver: no focal lesions. Gallbladder and bile ducts normal. Spleen normal in size. Adrenal glands unremarkable. Kidneys enhance symmetrically without hydronephrosis. No retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy. No ascites. Bowel unremarkable; appendix surgically absent. Lung bases clear. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: 3.4 cm arterially enhancing solid mass of the pancreatic tail, in the setting of elevated glucagon most consistent with a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (glucagonoma). No hepatic lesions or adenopathy.

documents.title: Imaging Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CT: 3.4 cm hypervascular pancreatic tail mass, no liver lesions or nodes. With glucagon 1,180, this is a glucagonoma until proven otherwise. Will call pt tomorrow AM when I can talk it through properly; refer surgical oncology.

documents.title: CT Results Discussion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Phone with pt and wife. Reviewed CT: single 3.4 cm mass in the tail of the pancreas, no sign of spread to liver or lymph nodes. Explained this is very likely the glucagon-producing tumor driving the rash, weight loss and high sugars, and that surgery is usually the treatment when it's localized like this. Referral to surgical oncology placed, urgent. Endo updated. He was quiet but appreciated the call; wants everything moving. Couldn't reach him yesterday, LVM.

documents.title: Referral Coordination
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Surgical oncology referral faxed with CT report, glucagon and derm letters. Consult scheduled 11/13 1:00 pm. Pt notified.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology practice. Seen 2025-11-06.

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for the update on Mr. Robinson. The elevated glucagon and pancreatic tail mass make a glucagonoma the working diagnosis, and he has a surgical oncology consultation next week.

Adrenal insufficiency: stable, same hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone doses. For surgery he will need stress-dose coverage: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV at induction, then 50 mg IV every 8 hours, tapering back to his usual oral doses over two to three days as he recovers. I have sent this to the surgical team.

Hyperglycemia: I expect this to improve after the tumor is removed. With resection the likely next step, we agreed to watch it without starting a medication; he knows the symptoms that should prompt a call.

With thanks,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Surgical Oncology Consultation
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Outside surgical oncology clinic. Seen 2025-11-13.

Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Robinson, 47, with a 3.4 cm arterially enhancing pancreatic tail mass, serum glucagon of 1,180 pg/mL and biopsy-supported necrolytic migratory erythema. Background: primary adrenal insufficiency on replacement, sarcoidosis, chronic anemia, remote appendectomy. NKDA.

Exam: thin, otherwise well. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed right lower quadrant scar. Skin findings as described by dermatology.

Imaging shows localized disease without hepatic involvement.

Recommendation: laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy. We discussed risks including pancreatic leak, bleeding, infection and conversion to open surgery. He wishes to proceed; surgery is planned for 12/9.

Pre-operative needs:
1. Vaccination against encapsulated organisms at least two weeks before surgery: pneumococcal conjugate and meningococcal ACWY. We would be grateful if your office could give these.
2. Stress-dose steroids per his endocrinologist's plan.

With thanks,
Surgical Oncology

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pre-splenectomy vaccines per surgical oncology letter and PCP order; surgery 12/9 (3 wk). Afebrile, no acute illness. No prior vaccine reactions.
Given: PCV20 L deltoid; MenACWY R deltoid. VISs provided.
Observed 15 min, no reaction. MenACWY dose 2 due in 8 weeks or more: flagged for February visit. Pt has wallet card listing doses.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, surgical oncology service.
Admitted 2025-12-09. Discharged 2025-12-12.

Procedure: laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy, 2025-12-09. No conversion. Estimated blood loss minimal. Drain placed at the pancreatic stump.

Indication: 3.4 cm pancreatic tail neuroendocrine tumor with markedly elevated glucagon and necrolytic migratory erythema.

Hospital course: Stress-dose hydrocortisone 100 mg IV at induction, then 50 mg IV every 8 hours on POD 0-1, reduced on POD 2 and back to his home oral hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone on POD 3. Hemodynamically stable throughout. Clear liquids POD 1, regular diet POD 2. Drain amylase low; drain removed POD 3. Glucose readings fell into the 100s-120s after resection without insulin. Pain controlled on oral medication. Ambulating independently.

Allergies: NKDA.

Discharge medications: hydrocortisone 15 mg on waking and 5 mg early afternoon; fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily; hydrocortisone 100 mg IM emergency kit; oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 one tablet every 6 hours as needed for severe pain, 12 tablets.

Asplenia: pre-operative vaccines given 11/18 at his PCP's office. MenACWY dose 2 due in February. Advised to seek care promptly for any fever.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; surgical oncology clinic in 6 weeks with repeat glucagon; final pathology to follow.

documents.title: Operative Note
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Procedure: laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal. Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV given at induction.
Findings: firm, well-circumscribed mass in the pancreatic tail without invasion of adjacent structures. Liver surface smooth, no visible lesions. No peritoneal disease. Spleen normal in appearance.
Technique: five ports. Lesser sac entered, splenic flexure mobilized. Pancreas divided proximal to the mass with a stapler; splenic artery and vein controlled. Specimen extracted in a bag through an extended port site. Drain left at the stump.
Complications: none. Specimen to pathology.

reports.text:
Specimen: distal pancreas and spleen.
Gross: distal pancreas 9.0 cm with a well-circumscribed tan mass in the tail measuring 3.4 cm, 1.2 cm from the closest parenchymal margin. Attached spleen 11.0 cm, unremarkable cut surface.
Microscopic: well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor with nested and trabecular architecture, uniform nuclei, no necrosis. Mitoses fewer than 2 per 2 mm2. Ki-67 index 2%. Immunohistochemistry: synaptophysin and chromogranin positive; glucagon positive in tumor cells. No lymphovascular or perineural invasion. Parenchymal and vascular margins negative. Eleven peripancreatic lymph nodes negative (0/11). Spleen without pathologic change.
reports.conclusion: Distal pancreas: well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor, WHO grade 1 (Ki-67 2%), 3.4 cm, glucagon immunopositive, margins negative, 0/11 lymph nodes; no lymphovascular invasion. Spleen: unremarkable.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Final path reviewed: WD NET G1, glucagon+, 3.4 cm, margins neg, 0/11 nodes. Good result. Will review with him at Thursday's post-discharge visit.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Lap distal pancreatectomy + splenectomy 12/9, home 12/12. Path: WD NET G1, glucagon+, 3.4 cm, margins neg, 0/11 LN.

Recovering. Pain mostly with getting up from bed, took 4 of the oxycodone tabs total, none in the last 3 days. Eating small meals, appetite returning. BMs normal. No fever. Back on usual hydrocortisone 15/5 and fludro 0.1 since POD3. Thirst gone. Rash already less angry, burning much better.

Meds reconciled with discharge list: no changes besides short oxycodone course.

Exam: afebrile. Port sites clean, dry, no erythema. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near extraction site. Skin: groin and lower abdominal plaque paler, less scale.

A/P
1. S/p distal pancreatectomy/splenectomy for glucagonoma: healing well. Surg onc f/u 1/22 with repeat glucagon.
2. Asplenia: PCV20 and MenACWY #1 given 11/18; MenACWY #2 at Feb visit. Counseled fever = same-day call or ED. Will need meningococcal boosters going forward; flagged.
3. Hyperglycemia: glucose today much better. Recheck in Feb.
4. Adrenal insufficiency: tolerated stress dosing, back on home doses.
5. Weight 71. Expect regain.

documents.title: Surgical Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Outside surgical oncology clinic. Seen 2026-01-22.

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Robinson is six weeks out from laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy for a 3.4 cm well-differentiated, grade 1 glucagon-secreting neuroendocrine tumor with negative margins and 0/11 nodes.

He is recovering well. The rash has cleared completely. Appetite is back and weight is climbing. No fevers.

Exam: incisions well healed. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin of the abdomen, groin and thighs clear.

Glucagon today is 74 pg/mL, now within the reference range.

Plan: surveillance with CT abdomen and pelvis at six months after surgery and clinic visit then, glucagon with each visit. He should continue asplenia precautions per your office.

With thanks,
Surgical Oncology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
2 mo after lap distal pancreatectomy/splenectomy for glucagonoma (WD NET G1, margins neg, 0/11). Surg onc 1/22: glucagon 74, normal; surveillance CT ~June.

Feels well. Rash completely gone, skin back to normal. No thirst, no dry mouth. Eating normally, weight 74 and rising. Back at work full time. No fevers since surgery.

Adrenal insufficiency: hydrocortisone 15/5, fludro 0.1. Endo in April.

Exam: well. Port scars healed. Abd soft NT. Skin clear, including groin and thighs.

A/P
1. Glucagonoma s/p resection: per surg onc surveillance.
2. NME resolved. Hyperglycemia resolved; CMP and A1c today to document. Weight loss resolved, regaining.
3. Asplenia: MenACWY #2 today. Fever plan reviewed again; he carries a card. Meningococcal booster in 5 yrs.
4. Chronic anemia: CBC today.
5. Adrenal insufficiency: stable.

RTC for physical in June.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glucose and A1c normal. LFTs normal now. Hgb 11.3, his usual. Platelets and WBC in range. Portal message sent.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology practice. Seen 2026-04-16.

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Robinson came through his pancreatic surgery in December without adrenal complications on the stress-dose plan. He feels well and his weight is recovering.

Blood pressure normal, no orthostatic symptoms. Sodium, potassium and glucose normal today.

Plan: continue hydrocortisone 15 mg on waking and 5 mg early afternoon and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily. Emergency kit renewed. Annual review here.

With thanks,
Endocrinology

events.reason: Surveillance CT after pancreatic NET resection

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Technique: multiphase CT of the abdomen and portal venous CT of the pelvis after IV contrast. Comparison: 2025-10-28.
Findings: Postsurgical changes of distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy with surgical clips at the pancreatic resection margin. No soft tissue mass or enhancing nodule at the resection bed. Remaining pancreas normal without ductal dilation. Liver without focal lesions. Adrenal glands unremarkable. No lymphadenopathy. No ascites or fluid collection. Bowel unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Expected postsurgical changes of distal pancreatectomy and splenectomy. No evidence of recurrent or metastatic disease.

documents.title: Surgical Oncology Surveillance
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
Outside surgical oncology clinic. Seen 2026-07-09.

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Robinson is seven months from resection of his grade 1 pancreatic glucagonoma. He feels well; skin remains clear and weight has recovered.

The June CT shows no recurrence. Exam unremarkable.

Plan: glucagon level next month (he can have it drawn at your office), then CT and clinic visit in six months.

With thanks,
Surgical Oncology
